newsitem.title: USA: Brophy heads First Albany's new proprietary group.
newsitem.headline: Brophy heads First Albany's new proprietary group.

text.p: First Albany Corp, a unit of First Albany Cos, has tapped bond market veteran Giles Brophy to head its new fixed-income proprietary group, an official at the firm said Monday.

Brophy, who began his new role August 11, most recently headed his own firm, New York-based Giles Securities, said Arthur Murphy, a senior vice president and director of First Albany's municipal division.
Earlier, Brophy also founded Brophy Gestal Knight, which was sold to Sanwa Bank, Murphy said. Brophy's municipal career has included time at Lehman Brothers and First Pennco.
Kerry Roche, formerly of Giles Securities, has also joined First Albany's new proprietary group as a principal. He will report to Brophy.

"Giles and Kerry are among the top people in the fixed income business," Murphy said. "We had been looking for the right people in this area and we've known Giles for a long time and we approached him."

Murphy said Brophy's debt markets experience will also bolster First Albany's growing focus on fixed-income product development for financial institution clients. First Albany is currently expanding its services in the community banking sector, he said.

Aside from its new fixed-income proprietary group, First Albany has also added staff on the municipal side. Gerard Walls joined the firm's institutional municipal sales group in late July. Previously, Walls served on the underwriting desk at Chemical Securities, which exited the municipal business in early 1996, Murphy said.
"He's got a wide range of experience in the municipal market, and we thought that he would be a real benefit to our institutional client base," Murphy said.

Also in July, First Albany hired Harry Tyson, one of the senior bankers in Dillon Read's New York office, he said. Dillon Read exited the muni business in June. Tyson has joined the firm as a senior vice president in public finance.
"Harry brings a wealth of experience from his years at Dillon Read and Smith Barney," Murphy said, adding that Tyson once headed up the public finance group at Smith Barney Inc.
